To find stationary points, first differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). Then, set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are where the function's slope is zero. Next, substitute these x-values back into f(x) to get the corresponding y-values, which gives you the stationary points. Lastly, use the second derivative test, if needed, to classify each point as a maximum, minimum, or saddle point.
